sections.title: Data We Collect
sections.body: We collect account details (name, email, organization name), tenant-bound workspace content (including prompts, agent and pipeline inputs, outputs, run records, steering messages, reports, and usage activity), and device details used for notifications (push token, platform, device name, and OS version). For Apple App Store or Google Play subscriptions, we retain the product, transaction or purchase token, receipt, status, and subscription dates. We do not receive raw card details; web billing is handled by Stripe.

sections.title: How We Use Your Data
sections.body: We process account and tenant-bound workspace data to provide requested platform features, run workflows, preserve workspace and run history, meter usage, manage entitlements, and support account operations. Content may be sent to AI providers selected or connected for a requested workflow; their handling is governed by the applicable provider terms and settings.

sections.title: Data Storage
sections.body: Account and device records remain user-bound, while workspace, activity, and subscription records remain tenant-bound, without a published fixed retention period. Deleting your user account removes your user record. If you are the tenant's last member, tenant workspace records are deleted through the account relationship; if other members remain, workspace content, activity, and store subscription records remain with that tenant. Notification-token removal on logout is best effort, and account deletion removes remaining user-bound devices.

sections.title: Third-Party Services
sections.body: We use Stripe for web billing; Apple App Store and Google Play for store billing; Expo for push delivery; SendGrid for transactional email; Google OAuth for optional authentication; and HubSpot for opt-in CRM integration. Sentry may receive crash, trace, and session diagnostic events. Each provider processes data under its own terms and settings.

sections.title: Your Rights
sections.body: You may request access, export, correction, or deletion by contacting privacy@braavolabs.com. Account deletion follows the tenant-membership behavior described above; cancelling a Stripe, Apple App Store, or Google Play subscription is a separate action. We will respond within 30 days.

sections.title: Security
sections.body: Our published web proxy configuration supports TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3 in transit. Other at-rest, production-access, security, and retention details are not promised here without current provider and deployment evidence.

sections.title: Changes
sections.body: We may update this policy from time to time. We will notify you of significant changes via email. Continued use of the platform after changes constitutes acceptance of the updated policy.

sections.title: Contact

sections.title: 1. Acceptance
sections.body: By creating an account or using Braavolabs, you agree to these Terms of Service. If you are using the platform on behalf of an organization, you represent that you have authority to bind that organization to these terms.

sections.title: 2. Service Description
sections.body: Braavolabs provides an AI-powered platform for creating and operating autonomous business workflows. When you request AI work, Braavolabs may send relevant workspace and run content to the provider or endpoint configured for that work. If you choose a remote endpoint, its operator may process that content under the applicable terms and settings.

sections.title: 3. Acceptable Use
sections.body: You may not use the platform to generate spam, conduct illegal activities, violate third-party rights, or circumvent the platform's governance and risk controls. Automated outreach is subject to anti-spam limits built into the platform.

sections.title: 4. Planned subscriptions
sections.body: Individual is planned at $19/month and Team at $39/active-user/month. Web checkout is not currently available and inference is not included. Any in-app offer is shown and sold through the applicable Apple App Store or Google Play listing.

sections.title: 5. Paid Plans
sections.body: Web subscriptions are billed through Stripe. In-app subscriptions are billed by Apple through the App Store or by Google through Google Play and are subject to that store's billing, cancellation, and refund rules. Manage or cancel in the channel where you subscribed. Cancellation does not itself delete your account or tenant workspace data.

sections.title: 6. Data Ownership
sections.body: You own all data you input into the platform, including company descriptions, agent configurations, and outputs. You grant us a limited license to process this data solely to provide the service.

sections.title: 7. AI Outputs
sections.body: AI-generated content (agent outputs, drafts, outreach messages) must be reviewed before sending. You are responsible for all content sent through integrations connected to your account.

sections.title: 8. Limitation of Liability
sections.body: The platform is provided 'as is'. We are not liable for indirect, incidental, or consequential damages arising from your use of the platform or AI-generated content.

sections.title: 9. Termination
sections.body: We may suspend or terminate accounts that violate these terms. You may delete your account at any time from the Settings page.

sections.title: 10. Contact

sections.title: What Cookies Are
sections.body: Cookies are small text files placed on your device when you visit a website. We use cookies and similar local storage techniques to keep you signed in, remember your language preference, and improve your experience.

sections.title: Cookies We Use
sections.body: Strictly necessary: a JWT session token for authentication. Preference: NEXT_LOCALE to remember your language. We do not run ad-targeting cookies. Analytics is opt-in (Plausible, cookie-less by default).

sections.title: Third-Party Cookies
sections.body: Stripe Checkout sets cookies during payment flows for fraud prevention. HubSpot tracking pixels run only if you opt in. Google or GitHub OAuth set their own cookies during sign-in — those are governed by their respective policies.

sections.title: How to Manage Cookies
sections.body: Most browsers allow you to refuse or delete cookies through their settings. Disabling strictly necessary cookies will prevent you from signing in. Where required, our cookie banner lets you accept or reject non-essential cookies.

sections.title: Legal Basis

getting-started.title: Getting started
getting-started.desc: Create a workspace, review a pipeline, and follow a governed run with explicit model and data choices.

0.text: Braavolabs combines a web workspace, desktop and CLI workbenches, and a mobile companion for model and agent work. Choose the model route and data mode deliberately before starting a run.

items.title: Sign in and describe the work
items.body: Create an account on the authenticated app. In the company builder, describe your goal, audience and constraints. The builder may ask clarifying questions before proposing a plan.

items.title: Review the proposal
items.body: Check the generated agents, pipeline steps, configured tools and expected outputs. Edit or remove anything you do not want. A proposed plan is not evidence that an external integration is connected.

items.title: Choose a route and start
items.body: Configure an available provider key or compatible local endpoint. Review its capabilities and data handling, then start the pipeline. Provider inference can incur charges when work begins.

items.title: Follow status and decisions
items.body: Read the recorded steps, available cost data, pending approvals and ask_user questions. Respond to the specific decision shown. You can send steering guidance or request a stop; an active call or external effect may already be in progress.

4.text: Individual ($19/month) and Team ($39/active user/month) are preview plan descriptions and are not currently available to purchase. Inference is separate: provider charges, local hardware and operation costs are not included.

5.text: Private Mode is a preview. Cloud Agent Mode and signed evidence remain in development. Holding is a premium/private preview. Do not treat these labels as a complete security or availability guarantee.

6.text: Use the web for composing companies and pipelines. Use the mobile companion to monitor, answer, approve and steer supported work.

concepts.title: Core concepts
concepts.desc: Understand companies, agents, pipelines, runs, decisions and recorded activity.

0.text: A company groups a goal, agents and pipelines inside your authenticated workspace. An agent performs a role; a pipeline orders work; a run is one execution of that pipeline. Multiple companies can belong to the same account or tenant.

2.text: The builder composes acquisition, sales, delivery, content, operations, finance, analytics, memory and governance roles. These are starting structures to review, not automatic permission to contact people, spend money or access an account.

4.text: Supported actions can produce pending approvals. An ask_user decision requests information rather than permission to spend. Read its question and scope before allowing, rejecting or answering. Provider inference is billed separately and does not necessarily wait for an approval row.

5.text: Governance checks include hard, loop, cost, spam and brand stops. Their coverage depends on the execution path and configuration. A stop prevents further supported work at a check boundary; it cannot retract an already sent request.

7.text: Activity and step records help explain status, outputs, available cost data and decision summaries. Missing data is unknown, not zero. A recorded request is not proof that its external effect completed. Retain important outputs and reconcile external systems before retrying uncertain work.

8.text: A company name or a local model endpoint alone does not establish a separate tenant, an operating-system sandbox or an offline-only data path.

byok-and-providers.title: BYOK & providers
byok-and-providers.desc: Configure a supported cloud or local model route and understand its cost and data boundaries.

0.text: Bring your own key (BYOK) means using your provider credentials for supported cloud inference. A compatible customer-operated endpoint is a separate route. Available providers and models come from the authenticated configuration; this page does not promise a fixed provider count.

items: Use a key scoped to the intended provider account. Review its provider-side spending controls and avoid putting secrets into prompts, shared logs or screenshots.
For a local endpoint, confirm its explicit base URL, supported model and reachability from the machine that will make the request.
Check model capabilities, tool support and the selected data mode. Changing providers can change output, price and behavior; a common API shape does not make models interchangeable.

3.text: Key storage depends on the surface

4.text: Server-stored cloud credentials use the implemented AES-256-GCM storage format. Protecting them also depends on the server key, runtime access and backups. CLI direct-provider configuration and desktop credential storage have their own boundaries; saving a key on one surface does not prove it is available or protected identically on every device.

5.text: Inference charges go to the configured provider. Local execution can still incur hardware and operation costs. Review reported usage and provider billing together; unavailable cost data is not zero-cost usage.

6.text: A local inference URL does not make tools, telemetry, account services or the complete pipeline offline. Review the complete data path before processing sensitive material.

mid-run-steering.title: Mid-run steering & ask_user
mid-run-steering.desc: Send guidance, answer a question, or request a stop while following the recorded run state.

0.text: Steering lets you send additional operator guidance to a supported run. State the change clearly: the intended customer, constraint or next step. The request is consumed at an available execution boundary, rather than guaranteeing an immediate interruption of an active provider call.

2.text: A successful request means the system accepted that request. It does not by itself prove the model received, applied or followed the instruction. Follow the subsequent run state and output. If a request fails or times out, inspect the current state before resubmitting.

4.text: When an agent requests information, open the matching pending decision and read the question and context. Submit the answer once, then check whether the decision and run state changed. Do not confuse an information request with authorization for an unrelated action.

6.text: Saved completed steps can be reused when work resumes. This does not establish exactly-once delivery for provider calls, emails, payments or other external effects. A pause, stop or failed connection can occur while an effect is in progress. Check recorded output and the external service before manually retrying uncertain work.

7.text: Pause, resume and steering do not guarantee zero additional cost or reverse an external effect that already happened.

webhooks.title: Webhooks
webhooks.desc: Sign a company webhook with the exact timestamp, raw body and header contract.

0.text: A configured company webhook accepts POST /hooks/<company-slug>/<event>. Use that company's configured webhook secret and a test company before sending an event that can start work.

2.text: Set X-Webhook-Timestamp to the current Unix time in milliseconds. Compute a hexadecimal HMAC-SHA256 over the timestamp, a literal dot, and the exact raw request body. Send it as X-Webhook-Signature. Do not reserialize or edit the body after signing.

3.caption: Example signed request; replace the API URL, company slug and event.

5.text: The server rejects timestamps outside a five-minute window. Signature-based duplicate detection uses Redis with a six-minute entry lifetime; when Redis is unavailable, signature and timestamp checks remain but that duplicate check can be skipped. This is not an exactly-once delivery guarantee.

6.text: A successful webhook response is not proof that the pipeline completed. Check run status and use application-level idempotency and reconciliation for external effects. Before retrying a timeout, inspect whether the first request was accepted.

external-automations.title: Connecting external automations
external-automations.desc: Connect a configured external automation and verify both sides of its execution.

0.text: Use configured integrations or signed webhooks to connect supported external automation tools. The availability and actions of an integration depend on its actual connection and credentials; naming n8n, Make or Zapier does not mean every workflow is automatically connected.

items.title: Choose the boundary
items.body: Decide which system starts work, which event it sends and which system owns the result. Connect only the account and permissions needed for that action.

items.title: Test with harmless data
items.body: Use a test company and an external test workflow. Verify the event payload, authentication, resulting run and external result.

items.title: Plan failure handling
items.body: Define timeouts, duplicate handling and a manual reconciliation step. Do not blindly resend a payment, email or other external effect after an uncertain response.

3.text: An external workflow status and a Braavolabs run status describe different parts of the operation. Check both. Recorded dispatch or a successful trigger response is not a delivery or completion receipt from the destination.

4.text: Connection credentials, webhook secrets and provider keys may have different storage and revocation paths. Review the relevant surface and external service when removing access.

mobile-app.title: Mobile app
mobile-app.desc: Use the mobile companion to monitor, decide and steer supported work.

0.text: The mobile app is a companion for supported monitoring and control. Compose companies and pipelines on the web, then use the phone to read run status, handle pending decisions and send steering guidance.

items: Monitor: open the relevant company and run. Treat unavailable or stale data as unknown; reconnect and refresh before making a decision.
Approve: read the specific pending action and allow or reject it. An approval row does not cover unrelated work or every provider charge.
Answer: respond to an ask_user question in its original context. Check the resulting decision state after submitting.
Steer: send a clear instruction and follow subsequent output. An accepted request is not proof that the instruction was applied.

4.text: Notifications depend on device permission, an eligible session, network access and delivery by the platform. Open the app to verify the latest state rather than treating a push notification as a complete execution record. Device-held session credentials use platform secure storage; protection and background behavior still depend on the device and operating system.

5.text: After switching accounts, confirm the selected company and pending decision again. On a timeout, inspect current state before retrying. The app cannot undo an external effect that already completed.

6.text: Choose your preferred language and light, dark or system theme in the app. After changing language or account, confirm the current workspace and decision context before acting.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.desc: Answers about previews, costs, local models, approvals and uncertain runs.

items.q: Can I buy a plan now?
items.a: Individual ($19/month) and Team ($39/active user/month) are preview descriptions and are not currently available to purchase. Inference is separate from the proposed subscription.

items.q: Does every charge require an approval?
items.a: No. Supported actions can require a pending decision, but provider inference can incur charges when a run starts. Read the action and provider spending controls before running work.

items.q: Does a local model make the platform offline?
items.a: No. A compatible local endpoint controls that inference route. Tools, account services, telemetry and other pipeline steps require their own data-path review.

items.q: Will resume repeat an external action?
items.a: Saved completed steps can be reused, but exactly-once external delivery is not established. Check the run and external service before retrying uncertain work.

items.q: Did an accepted steering request change the model output?
items.a: Acceptance records the request. Follow the next execution boundary and output to determine whether the instruction was applied and followed.

items.q: Can I build a complete company on my phone?

items.a: Private Mode is a preview; Cloud Agent Mode and signed evidence are in development. Their names are not a complete security or availability guarantee.

items.a: Do not assume it does. Check the subscription provider and any external service separately, and preserve required exports before deleting data.

steer-agents-mid-run.title: Steering a run without starting over
steer-agents-mid-run.desc: How operator guidance and saved steps help redirect supported work, and where their guarantees end.
steer-agents-mid-run.body:
A run can need a correction after it has started: a different customer, a tighter constraint, or a question the original brief did not answer. Braavolabs supports steering guidance and ask_user decisions so the operator can respond in context.

## A request has stages

Submitting guidance, accepting the request, consuming it at an execution boundary and following it in the output are different events. An active provider call can continue before the next boundary. Read the later run state and result before concluding that an instruction took effect.

## Preserve useful work, inspect uncertain work

Resuming can reuse saved completed steps. It does not prove exactly-once delivery for external effects, and it does not guarantee zero additional provider cost. If a connection fails during a send or payment, check the destination before manually retrying.

## Ask rather than infer permission

An ask_user decision requests information. A separate supported action can request approval. Read the scope of each decision: an answer to a question is not permission for unrelated work. These controls help make a working session inspectable; their presence does not establish that every route or external tool has identical behavior.

five-risk-stops-explained.title: The five risk stops and their boundaries
five-risk-stops-explained.desc: Hard, loop, cost, spam and brand checks help govern supported execution paths.
five-risk-stops-explained.body:
Braavolabs names five governance checks: hard, loop, cost, spam and brand. Understanding their purpose also means understanding when they can act.

## Five checks

The hard stop checks a stop condition. The loop check looks for repeated behavior. The cost check compares recorded usage with configured limits. Spam and brand checks apply policy to supported outreach and content paths. Review the configuration and execution path rather than assuming every tool receives the same checks.

## Boundaries matter

A check can prevent further supported work when the execution reaches it. It cannot recall a request already sent to a provider or reverse an external effect. Usage records can arrive after a charge, so a configured budget is not a guarantee that the provider bill can never exceed it.

## Read the result

When a check changes run state, inspect the recorded reason and relevant step. Missing status or cost data is unknown, not evidence that the run is safe or without cost. Notifications depend on permission and delivery; the current run record is the place to confirm state. Before resuming, review both the local result and any external service involved.

byok-routing-without-lock-in.title: Choosing cloud and local model routes
byok-routing-without-lock-in.desc: Keep provider choice explicit while checking capabilities, costs and credential boundaries.
byok-routing-without-lock-in.body:
Braavolabs supports configured cloud credentials and compatible customer-operated endpoints. The useful promise is an explicit route choice, not that every model is interchangeable or that an unmeasured model is always best.

## Check the route you choose

Review the available model, tool support, data mode and endpoint reachability. A provider change can change output quality, latency, price and supported parameters. If a selected route is unavailable, inspect the error rather than assuming a different model silently completed the work.

## Separate subscription and inference

The proposed Individual and Team subscriptions do not include inference. Provider charges belong to the configured account; local models still require hardware and operation. Compare reported usage with provider billing. Unknown cost is not zero cost.

## Protect the relevant credential store

Server-stored cloud keys use the implemented AES-256-GCM format. Server key protection, runtime access and backups still matter. CLI direct-provider configuration and desktop credential storage have separate boundaries. Review the store that actually makes the request, and revoke access in the provider as well when necessary. A common interface helps organize work; it does not establish identical security or economics across routes.

pocket-steering.title: Monitor and decide from your phone
pocket-steering.desc: The mobile companion focuses on supported monitoring, approvals, questions and steering.
pocket-steering.body:
The mobile companion provides a smaller control surface for work composed on the web. Its core actions are reading run state, handling a pending approval, answering ask_user and sending steering guidance.

## Keep the decision in context

Open the relevant company and run before acting. Read the exact question or action, and distinguish an information request from permission for an external effect. Provider inference can already incur charges without a separate approval row.

## Treat delivery and state separately

Push notifications depend on device permission, session eligibility, network access and platform delivery. A notification can be delayed; refresh the app to confirm the current decision. A successful steering response records acceptance of the request, not proof that the model followed it.

## Recover carefully

After an account switch or interrupted connection, confirm the selected account, company and pending decision again. Inspect current state before resubmitting a timeout. A mobile action cannot retract an external request that already completed. Platform secure storage helps protect device-held session credentials, while physical-device, background-delivery and cross-account tests remain necessary release checks.

local-model-routing-boundaries.title: Local model routing boundaries
local-model-routing-boundaries.desc: A local inference endpoint is one part of the complete data path.
local-model-routing-boundaries.body:
A compatible customer-operated model server can be configured with an explicit base URL. Braavolabs does not bundle a model or infer a complete privacy policy from the address alone.

## Trace the whole operation

Check which machine makes the inference call, which model is available and whether the endpoint is reachable from that machine. Then inspect the tools, account services, telemetry, logs and other steps that can still use a network connection. A local URL does not make the complete pipeline offline.

## Review capabilities and cost

Model capabilities and tool support can differ from cloud routes. Review outputs after changing a route. Local inference may remove a provider token charge for that call, but hardware, electricity, maintenance and other connected services still have costs. Missing cost data should remain unknown.

## Keep preview labels precise

Private Mode is a preview. Cloud Agent Mode and signed evidence remain in development. Those labels do not establish a complete data-handling contract, an operating-system sandbox or independently verified evidence. Sensitive use requires checking the actual configured data path and execution permissions.

shipping-ask-user.title: Designing ask_user around a clear question
shipping-ask-user.desc: An information request should preserve context and avoid implying unrelated permission.
shipping-ask-user.body:
An agent can encounter missing information while working. ask_user gives that uncertainty a visible decision: a question for the operator, associated with the relevant run.

## Ask one answerable question

A useful question identifies the missing fact and enough context to answer it. It should not disguise an external action as a request for information. Read the question before responding, and keep sensitive credentials out of open-text answers.

## Reuse the decision surface carefully

Information requests and supported approval actions can appear in the same decision workflow, but they have different meanings. Answering a question is not authorization for unrelated work. Nor does the presence of an approval queue mean every provider inference charge waits for an explicit yes.

## Check what happens next

After sending an answer, inspect the decision and run state. A received answer, a resumed run and a completed external effect are separate observations. If the connection times out, check whether the answer was recorded before resubmitting. Saved completed steps can be reused, but external retries still require reconciliation. This is a design rationale for a visible operator decision, not a measured customer study or a claim of exactly-once execution.

audit-trail-youd-actually-read.title: Reading the recorded activity of a run
audit-trail-youd-actually-read.desc: Use recorded status, outputs, decisions and available costs without inventing missing evidence.
audit-trail-youd-actually-read.body:
An operator needs to understand what a run attempted, which decisions were requested and what result was recorded. Braavolabs activity and step views organize those records around the run.

## Start with the recorded facts

Read the step status, available output, recorded decision summary and any reported cost. Keep unavailable values visibly unknown. A dispatch record or successful API acknowledgement does not prove that an external message, payment or workflow completed.

## Reconcile before retrying

A provider or tool can finish while a client loses its connection. Compare the run record with the destination service before repeating an uncertain external effect. Saved steps and history are useful evidence, but they do not establish complete, immutable or independently verified coverage of every action.

## Protect the record

Prompts, tool outputs and open-text answers can contain sensitive data. Limit access and preserve only the exports needed for your operation. Review retention, backups and restoration rather than assuming a visible activity page is a backup. Signed evidence remains in development; the current record should not be presented as a certification, a complete private reasoning trace or proof of legal compliance.

content-studio.title: Content Studio
content-studio.desc: Spot trends, draft, and polish social posts on autopilot.
content-studio.seed: I run a small brand and want a content studio that publishes consistently. A trend scout should find 2-3 angles trending in my niche, a writer should draft a TikTok and a LinkedIn post for the strongest angle, and an editor should tighten the hook and CTA. Save each as a draft for me to review before posting, and remember which angles performed so future drafts get sharper.

content-repurposer.title: Content Repurposer
content-repurposer.desc: Turn one idea into an X thread, a LinkedIn post, and a newsletter blurb.
content-repurposer.seed: I want to repurpose one source idea, post, or transcript into a multi-platform pack. A strategist should pick the three strongest angles, then a writer should spin them into an X thread, a LinkedIn post, and a short newsletter blurb — all in my brand voice if it's stored in memory. Save the pack as a draft.

seo-content-engine.title: SEO Content Engine
seo-content-engine.desc: Research keywords and outline search-optimized articles.
seo-content-engine.seed: I want an SEO content engine. A researcher should find the search intent and related questions for a target keyword, an outliner should produce an H2/H3 structure with internal-link suggestions, and a writer should draft a search-optimized article around it. Save the brief and draft, and remember which topics I've already covered so we don't repeat ourselves.

newsletter-studio.title: Newsletter Studio
newsletter-studio.desc: Curate a theme and draft a weekly newsletter issue.
newsletter-studio.seed: I send a weekly newsletter and want help drafting each issue. A curator should pick a theme and gather 3-5 worth-sharing items for my audience, then a writer should draft the issue with a strong subject line, intro, the curated items with one-line takes, and a closing CTA. Save it as a draft and remember past themes so issues stay varied.

podcast-repurposer.title: Podcast Repurposer
podcast-repurposer.desc: Turn an episode transcript into show notes and clip-worthy quotes.
podcast-repurposer.seed: I host a podcast and want to repurpose each episode. Given a transcript, a producer should write structured show notes with timestamps and key takeaways, and a clip-finder should surface 5-8 quotable moments worth turning into short social clips. Save the notes and the quote list as drafts.

brand-voice-builder.title: Brand Voice Builder
brand-voice-builder.desc: Codify your tone into a one-page reference doc.
brand-voice-builder.seed: I want to codify my brand voice. A brand analyst should extract tone attributes, signature phrases, and phrases to avoid from a description and any sample content I provide, then a style codifier should write a one-page reference with three example posts that demonstrate the voice. Store it in memory under 'brand voice' so my content agents can read it.

competitor-watch.title: Competitor Watch
competitor-watch.desc: Track rival moves and summarize what changed each week.
competitor-watch.seed: I want to keep an eye on a handful of competitors. A web researcher should scan for recent moves — launches, pricing changes, messaging shifts — across their sites and the web, then an analyst should summarize what changed this week and why it matters for my positioning. Save a short report and remember prior findings so each scan only flags what's new.

social-listening.title: Social Listening
social-listening.desc: Surface what people are saying about a topic or brand.
social-listening.seed: I want social listening on a topic and my brand. A researcher should gather recent public mentions and discussions across the web, then an analyst should cluster them into themes, flag the sentiment, and pull a few representative quotes. Save a digest and store recurring themes in memory so trends become visible over time.

webinar-promoter.title: Webinar Promoter
webinar-promoter.desc: Plan a promo sequence for an upcoming event.
webinar-promoter.seed: I have a webinar coming up and want a promotion plan. A planner should map a multi-touch promo timeline (announce, value teaser, reminder, last-call), then a writer should draft the social posts and emails for each touch in my brand voice. Save everything as drafts for me to schedule manually.

ad-creative-tester.title: Ad Creative Tester
ad-creative-tester.desc: Generate ad angle variations to test, no spend.
ad-creative-tester.seed: I want to test ad creative angles before spending. A strategist should propose 4-5 distinct angles (pain, outcome, social-proof, contrarian, curiosity) for my product, then a copywriter should write a headline and primary text variant for each. Save them as drafts so I can paste the winners into my ad platform myself. No ad spend or platform writes.

outreach-strategist.title: Outreach Strategist
outreach-strategist.desc: Sharpen your ICP and draft a cold-email sequence.
outreach-strategist.seed: I want a cold-outreach engine that drafts but never sends. An ICP researcher should sharpen my ideal customer profile from my product and a target hint, then a pitch writer should produce a three-message sequence — intro, follow-up, and breakup — ready to copy into my inbox. Save the sequence as a draft.

cold-outreach-engine.title: Cold Outreach Engine
cold-outreach-engine.desc: Personalize first-touch emails for a target list.
cold-outreach-engine.seed: I have a list of target accounts and want personalized first-touch emails. A researcher should pull a relevant hook for each prospect from public info, then a writer should draft a short, specific opener referencing that hook with one clear CTA. Save drafts for me to review and send manually, and log every draft. No automatic sending.

lead-qualifier.title: Lead Qualifier
lead-qualifier.desc: Score inbound leads against your ICP and route them.
lead-qualifier.seed: I want to qualify inbound leads. Given a lead's details, an analyst should score fit against my ICP (industry, size, role, intent signals) and a router should recommend an action — fast-track, nurture, or disqualify — with a one-line reason. Log every decision and remember scoring patterns so qualification gets more consistent over time.

proposal-writer.title: Proposal Writer
proposal-writer.desc: Turn a project brief into a client-ready proposal.
proposal-writer.seed: I want to turn a project brief into a client proposal. A scoper should sharpen the client context, problem, success metrics, and scope boundaries, then a writer should draft a structured proposal — summary, scope, deliverables, phased timeline, and value-framed pricing. Save it as a draft for me to review and send.

partnership-outreach.title: Partnership Outreach
partnership-outreach.desc: Find fitting partners and draft intro pitches.
partnership-outreach.seed: I want to line up partnership conversations. A researcher should identify the kinds of companies that complement my product and find a few concrete candidates, then a writer should draft a tailored intro pitch for each that leads with the mutual win. Save the pitches as drafts for me to send manually.

market-research.title: Market Research Agent
market-research.desc: Scan a market and synthesize a one-page report.
market-research.seed: I want a fast market scan. A web researcher should gather signals across 5-10 high-signal sources about my market, then a synthesizer should produce a one-page report covering market size signals, the top three competitors with a one-line distinction each, 12-month trends, and the opportunity. Save the report and store key findings in memory so future scans build on them.

customer-onboarding.title: Customer Onboarding
customer-onboarding.desc: Draft a guided welcome sequence for new customers.
customer-onboarding.seed: I want to onboard new customers smoothly. A planner should map a milestone-based onboarding journey (welcome, setup, first value, check-in), then a writer should draft the message for each milestone in my brand voice. Save the sequence as drafts I can send manually, and remember the journey so every new customer gets the same guided start.

churn-watch.title: Churn Watch
churn-watch.desc: Flag at-risk accounts and draft win-back outreach.
churn-watch.seed: I want to catch churn early. Given account activity I provide, an analyst should flag at-risk accounts with the warning signs and a reason, then a writer should draft a tailored win-back message for each flagged account. Save drafts for me to review, log every assessment, and remember which signals tend to precede churn.

product-launch-kit.title: Product Launch Kit
product-launch-kit.desc: Assemble launch messaging and a go-live checklist.
product-launch-kit.seed: I'm launching a product and want a launch kit. A strategist should draft the core positioning and key messages, a writer should produce the announcement assets (landing copy, social posts, launch email), and an ops agent should assemble a go-live checklist. Save everything as drafts and keep the checklist in memory so nothing slips.

invoice-chaser.title: Invoice Chaser
invoice-chaser.seed: I want help chasing overdue invoices. Given a list of outstanding invoices I provide, an agent should draft a polite, escalating reminder for each (gentle nudge, firm follow-up, final notice) referencing the amount and due date. Save the reminders as drafts for me to send manually, and log every draft. Never send anything automatically and never move money.

weekly-finance-digest.title: Weekly Finance Digest
weekly-finance-digest.desc: Summarize the numbers I track into a weekly readout.
weekly-finance-digest.seed: I want a weekly finance digest. Given the figures I provide (revenue, spend, runway, key metrics), an analyst should compare them to the prior period, call out what moved and why it matters, and flag anything that needs attention. Save a short readout and remember prior weeks so the digest shows trends. Read-only — no transactions.

support-triage.title: Support Triage
support-triage.desc: Categorize tickets and draft first replies.
support-triage.seed: I want to triage incoming support tickets. Given a ticket, an agent should categorize it (bug, billing, how-to, feature request), set a priority, and draft a helpful first reply grounded in my knowledge base. Save the draft for a human to review before sending, log every triage decision, and remember recurring issues so common answers improve.

review-responder.title: Review Responder
review-responder.desc: Draft on-brand replies to customer reviews.
review-responder.seed: I want help responding to customer reviews. Given a review, an agent should gauge the sentiment and draft a thoughtful, on-brand reply — gracious for praise, accountable and solution-oriented for complaints. Save replies as drafts for me to post, and remember recurring praise and complaints so I can spot patterns.

recruiting-sourcer.title: Recruiting Sourcer
recruiting-sourcer.desc: Draft a role profile and personalized candidate outreach.
recruiting-sourcer.seed: I'm hiring and want sourcing help. A recruiter agent should turn a role into a sharp candidate profile (must-haves, signals, where they hang out), then a writer should draft a warm, personalized outreach message I can send to promising candidates. Save drafts for me to send manually and log every one. No automatic messaging.
